title: The resort owner's quarrels and the Phoenix offer
summary: The older white owner and his young wife fought, he was put out, and he offered the band a Phoenix job; Eddie Hill, apparently involved with the wife, would not go.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: That's true. Yes, it is. So we stayed

out there in Albuquerque and it was going pretty nice with the exception, the fella that we was playing for, he and his wife, they -- she was really a young woman, she was a young woman and he was an older fella. And they used to kind of spat, you know, this white couple, you know, and they'd kind of have these spats and sometimes, I remember one time he got so mad at her, he started to cut her with a knife and we grabbed him, you know. "Oh, don't do that. Don't do that." You know. So then he used to talk to me a lot. He'd say, "I'll tell you what," he says, "Now, I know that I was acting up the other night. But don't pay that too much attention. I probably had a few hits there," he says, "you know, when I'm kind of acting up, I'm glad that you guys did talk to me." I said, "Well, we didn't want you to hurt her," you know, and so forth.

So then she got mad and put him out and he moved in town, Albuquerque. So he moved in town and so he -- when I'd go in town, sometime he'd call me up. He knew where I'd stop when I'd go in town. He'd call me up and say, "Look, how are things going out to the club?" I'd say, "Things are going pretty good." He'd say, "Well, I'll tell you what I want you guys to do. I want you guys -- I got a club I can put you all in in Phoenix. I want you all to leave that club. That place ain't no good out there. I want you to get away from there." I say, "Okay, well, listen, I'll tell Eddie to get in touch with you right away, because I'd like to go to Phoenix. I've never
been to Phoenix, you know." He said, "Well, you tell Eddie to get in touch with me." So, okay, I told Eddie. I think Eddie was kind of sweet on the girl, the old lady, see what I mean?
Yeah.

So Eddie ain't about to go nowhere. So the old man called me and said, "Did you tell Eddie?" I said, "Yeah, I told him." I says, "I tell you what. If Eddie don't want to go, you just -- you give the gig to me and I'll tell the rest of the guys. We'll make the gig."

So the old man says, "Well, if he don't call in pretty soon, I might just do that. I'll just give the gig to the rest of you guys and you all can go and make a date." So this friend of his, he said, had a club out there. Well, so, we had a big doings out there one night. Oh, the place was just loaded from front to back.
How big a place was it?
It was a big place.
I mean the resort.
The resort? Well, the resort, actually, the only thing that was happening at the resort, they had like adobe houses and where people could -- you know what I mean?
Were they up there riding houses and things?
No, they didn't have no horse riding.
Oh, it wasnt a dude ranch.
The only thing we had to offer was dancing, booze and the club.
Oh, I see. So it was like a sneak-away place.
Yeah.
I got you.
But it was a big place, you know, and the old man quite naturally, you know, he was crazy about this young woman and he had -- you know what I mean -- spent a lot of money on this place.
Yeah, yeah.

So we had this big doings there and oh, boy, just people from everywhere were there. So we got through playing that night and I decided to go in town, you know, and I went on in town. So the old man called me that next morning and he says, "Hey, how was things out at the club last night?" I says, "Oh, they was jumping. It was great." He says, "Well, now, listen, I'll tell you. You didn't have no trouble out there?" I says, "No, there wasn't no trouble." He says, "Well, I heard there had been some trouble out there." He says, "I figured I'd call you and check you out to see if there was." I said, "No, no, there wasn't no trouble." He says, "Okay," and he hung up. He went out on to the club.
